notes.title: Little Big Adventure – Twinsen’s Quest – Patch Note – December 2024
notes.content:
[h2]Patch 1.1.1[/h2]

The patch notes are ready, and the update is just around the corner. Thanks for your support and patience!

[h3]Technical changes[/h3]

[list]
[*] Steam is now automatically launched if the game is started from Desktop
[*] Add Graphics Settings panel
[*] Fix of wide screen UI Layouts
[/list]

[h3]Gamefeel and systems[/h3]

[list]
[*] Dodge animation is no more interrupted by hits (Damages still apply)
[*] Fix of Twinsen being blocked in fall animation and/or landing after being hit
[*] Fix repeated jump or dodge after being hit
[*] Fix Saber Animations after being hit
[*] Mouse melee, aim and throw now attack in the direction of a locked target instead of the mouse cursor
[*] Mouse cursor is now greyed when target is locked.
[*] Lock & Unlock are now enabled while aiming
[*] Fix rotating while throwing MagicBall
[*] Fix locked mouse cursor not cleared when unlocking by distance
[*] Twinsen now uses a clover if any left when drowning or falling, instead of a Game Over
[/list]

[h3]UI[/h3]

[list]
[*] Fix an issue where the dodge animation was played when exiting Holomap
[*] Fix Fuel Count in inventory when quantity was superior to 99 units
[*] Fix description of some items in the inventory
[*] New Save slot is now selected by default in the Saves menu
[*] Adventure Log can now be opened from inventory
[*] Addition of an animation to selected Save Game
[*] Addition of a preview of the items when obtained.
[*] Update Main Menu background image
[*] Fix an issue where “???” was displayed in the Loading menu
[/list]

[h3]Audio[/h3]

[list]
[*] Fix of a duplicated running jump sound
[*] Fix jump sound being repeated after falling
[*] Fix Music stopped after ending the game.
[*] Fix Lulu hit sound when running
[*] Update and fix some voices.
[*] Update music volumes
[*] Fix Protopack drowning animation loop, that caused duplicated drown sound.
[/list]

[h3]Diverse changes & fixes[/h3]

[u]Citadel Island[/u]
[list]
[*] Improve asylum secret pipe sequence
[*] Improvements on Zoe’s path in Chapter 0
[*] Luna now throws another ball if Twinsen doesn’t have one for 5s in the Boingball sequence
[*] Fix Twinsen’s house access through the chimney
[*] Fix Twinsen stucked after leaving its cave to go outside
[*] Change of the boingball basket’s collider in Luna’s room.
[*] Fix an issue where the Groboclone in the Pharmacy was rotating around its destination
[/list]
[u]Principal Island[/u]
[list]
[*] Fix chair blocking Pages in the library
[*] Add interaction hint to pour water in the Water Tower
[*] Improvements of the sequence of the painting secret passage
[*] Remove duplicated Telepods in FunFrock’s headquarters
[*] Improvements on the FunFrock Headquarters secret exit sequence
[*] Improvements on Jean escaping from FunFrock HQ sequence
[*] Fix Water wave height on Port-Belooga
[*] Fix Library sign that displayed no text
[*] Fix Prison white groboclone duplicated model
[*] Fix an issue where Twinsen was saying a line instead of Victoire
[/list]
[u]Desert Island[/u]
[list]
[*] Fix of a logic issue where the catamaran was present on desert island when not bought yet.
[*] Fix of the talking hint on the tank
[*] Fix blades in Temple of Bù that were moved up if hit by a projectile.
[/list]
[u]Proxima Island[/u]
[list]
[*] Fix logic issue where the Ancestral Key could be stolen before getting the red card
[*] Fix manhole entrances
[*] Museum: Change on the shortcut to exit after stealing the treasure
[*] Fix the shop items hint to interact
[*] Fix Boris’ path in shop
[*] Ruby now doesn’t give the flag if the catamaran is already equipped
[*] Fix of Ruby’s dialog in the cavern
[*] A collision has been added to avoid jumping above the Golden Door
[*] Addition of Protopack limits on Proxima-East
[/list]
[u]Rebel Island[/u]
[list]
[*] Bombs now do not lock Twinsen
[/list]
[u]Hamalayi[/u]
[list]
[*] Improvements of Lightning pathfinding, that could previously lead to unwanted blockers.
[*] Add Interaction hint to Fortin’s exit pipe
[*] Fix Lightning running when Twinsen is on the top of the building near the radar.
[/list]
[u]Mutant[/u]
[list]
[*] Fix softlock when Carotina wasn’t showing 
[*] Fix invisible wall in Mutant Factory
[*] Add interaction hint to Carrot soup to trigger Carotina
[/list]
[u]Tippett Island[/u]
[list]
[*] Add Protopack limits to arrival scene
[*] Fix issue with the Dino-Fly options
[*] Fix a lock that happened after talking to Agnetha
[*] Adjustments of the ladders in the Tippett sewers.
[/list]
[u]Brundle Island[/u]
[list]
[*] The Telepod can no more be activated once the teleport center is destroyed
[*] Adjustments of ladders on Brundle Island
[/list]
[u]Polar Island[/u]
[list]
[*] Fix of a hole in building roof
[*] Fix hole in construction site
[*] Bulldozer speed has been reduced, except Twinsen’s one.
[*] Add Twinsen’s missing voiceline when close to rebels
[*] Fix an issue where Twinsen falls from the platform activated by Zoe
[*] Fix Mushrooms on the whole island
[*] The Saber has been removed from FunFrock’s model.
[/list]

notes.title: 🎥 Announcement Teaser
notes.content:
Dear Community,

In May 2023, we presented the first images of our game. One year later, many things have evolved:

[list]
[*] We changed the game engine,
[*] We signed with a publisher,
[*] We shifted from a remaster to a remake,
[*] We recruited a full team (and worked hard)!
[/list]

We are now proud to present the all-new first images of the LBA remake! Help us make some noise by sharing, liking and commenting the video:

[previewyoutube=kuuPRptsSww;full][/previewyoutube]

We want to warmly thank our publisher Microids, who believed in us from day one and is helping us bring Twinsen back to life. We are happy to announce that you will be able to find [i]Little Big Adventure – Twinsen’s Quest[/i] on PC, PS4, PS5, Nintendo Switch, Xbox One, and Xbox Series!

We will also offer a physical edition for PS5 and Nintendo Switch.

What do you think of this very first trailer? Feel free to let us know in the comments.

We can’t wait to show you more.

Ben

notes.title: One of Our Biggest Challenges: Geographic Continuity
notes.content:
Dear community,

It’s time for us to share one of our biggest challenges with this remake: outdoor geographic continuity. What are we talking about?

Remember: in the original game, the exteriors were divided into “cubes” for technical reasons (memory, performance, etc.). Four “black borders” defined the limits of each cube. At certain places, it was possible to change cubes. This system is difficult for players to understand today and was already abandoned in 1997 for [i]Little Big Adventure 2/Twinsen’s Odyssey[/i]. Our vision for the remake? To merge these cubes to create a more immersive open world. Easy, right? Well, not exactly. There are 3 major difficulties:

[b]1/ Joining cubes… that don’t fit together
[/b]
Some cubes respect the geographic topography and can be correctly merged. Example: Brundle Island.

[url=https://twinsenslittlebigadventure.com/en/one-of-our-biggest-challenges-geographic-continuity/][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43801523/680dd2efd6286b5c52b73d5763386800cc7e0abc.png[/img]
[/url]
Some cubes are logical and go together, but have an altitude difference that creates a problem. Example: Citadel Island. How to manage the altitude difference between the 2 cubes?

[url=https://twinsenslittlebigadventure.com/en/one-of-our-biggest-challenges-geographic-continuity/][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43801523/302ad2c9b28f336382d4a85f3727a9d104fedc36.png[/img]
[/url]
Some original cubes simply do not connect at all. The biggest example is Principal Island. Some cubes negatively impact the cube next to it. On Principal Island, the building of the HQ prevents visibility of the Twinsen character when one wishes to go to the library. Here, we thus need to shift the library cube to keep the path readable.

What happens if we unite the cubes of Principal Island?

[url=https://twinsenslittlebigadventure.com/en/one-of-our-biggest-challenges-geographic-continuity/][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43801523/20f4dcc9f4f6632a39ec7d8812c3aceb502d53b6.png[/img]
[/url]
[olist]
[*] A path is missing between the library and the military camp
[*] The HQ hides part of the path on the 3 cubes next to it
[*] The old town hides part of the path from the military camp cube
[/olist]
Obviously, we cannot leave Funfrock’s HQ as is in a game with continuity. Transforming it into a real building worsens the visibility problems on the adjacent cubes. It’s a real puzzle!

We decided to create new spaces – internally called “seams” – to join the cubes in a more organic way.

[b]2/ Replacing black borders with content
[/b]
Once the cubes are united, we need to find a graphical way to replace the black walls with content. In the Proxima Island prototype, we simply placed trees, but it’s not always that simple.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43801523/cfdff2a9a7d77c357ec064e03ec0a2ee0495bcae.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43801523/5e517b950da1dc802234bc6d76a546128ef39f16.jpg[/img]

[b]3/ Story coding
[/b]
We’ve talked about the tip of the iceberg. Let’s move on to the submerged part. The original code is based on cube logic. When loading a cube, the code checks what you have in your inventory to define the state of that cube. The NPCs’ routines also start at this moment. What happens when the cubes are united? The routines start when you arrive on the island (and not the cube). The most complex case: when you are in a vehicle (the tank in the Hamalayi and the bulldozer on Polar Island). Here, you change cubes while in the vehicle. Seb tore out the last hairs he had 🤯.

Another example: to give a sense of life in the original game, you could meet the same NPC several times in different cubes of the same island. For example, you meet the hair dryer salesman several times on Citadel Island. By uniting the cubes, we end up with… multiple hair dryer salesmen! We need to keep one and create a new routine for the character so that he traverses the equivalent of several cubes from the original game.

The most complex case is when a character follows Twinsen from one cube to another (e.g., the rebel lapichon in the Hamalayi). Physically, these are different NPCs, reset at each cube change with their own code. Again, we had to be clever to make it seem like it’s now the same one following you from cube to cube!

[b]The most frustrating
[/b]
We believe geographic continuity is one of the changes that will allow the game to be discovered by the largest number of people. The most frustrating thing for us is that even you, the fans, won’t notice it. Our memories have built an idealized version of the original game that was a true open-world. To succeed, we have to do better than your memories 😅

In my childhood memories, I always believed I had a gun that shot red lasers in [i]Little Big Adventure 2/Twinsen’s Odyssey[/i]… but no!

We hope this significant change will allow you to relive the emotions of your childhood… without realizing it 😃

notes.title: Behind the Scenes of the Remake
notes.content:
Dear Community,

Today, we invite you on an exclusive journey behind the scenes of our remake. Let’s start with a look back:

In June 2023, you experienced an initial prototype on Proxima Island, developed in a short time by a small team. Despite its imperfections, this prototype was a crucial springboard for engaging with you and understanding your expectations.

This prototype was built using Unreal Engine 5, with an almost manual reconstruction of the island. Faced with the challenge of replicating this method for a larger world in a limited time, we opted for a complete overhaul of the game, based on new foundations. But what is the nature of these new foundations?

The answer lies in the work of Sébastien Viannay, a developer on the original games, as well as the mobile port. It was during the work on the latter that Seb developed a small tool to setup the pathfinding – that is, the ability to tap a point on the screen and have Twinsen follow that direction. This tool interprets the original game’s data to reconstruct the level and identify obstacles.

This tool opened a new world for us: using the original game’s data in a modern game engine. In practice, all the game logic (quests, dialogues, levels, even animations) is in the form of data. By importing it into a new engine, we can not only faithfully reproduce the game but also reinvent it.

The only hiccup in this story? Seb developed this tool on Unity 😅. After attempting to transfer this tool to Unreal, we made the strategic decision to migrate to Unity during last summer.

[h3]How We Are Developing the Remake
[/h3]
Our adventure thus continues on Unity, leveraging the original data. Here are the key steps of our project:

[olist]
[*] [b]Transposition of the Original Game into Unity:[/b] Our goal is to preserve the essence and logic of the original game. One of the major challenges lies in adapting the original scenes to geographical continuity, an aspect we will detail in a dedicated article.
[*] [b]Drawing Inspiration from the Unreal Prototype to Perfect Twinsen’s Movements and Controls:[/b] We aim to enhance the gameplay experience while remaining true to the original.
[*] [b]Enriching the Narrative:[/b] We plan to adjust certain sequences of the game, such as reducing the repetitive back-and-forth between the Northern and Southern hemispheres.
[*] [b]Reconstruction of the Islands in 3D with a New Art Direction:[/b] We are reimagining the islands to offer a unique visual experience.
[*] [b]Recreation of All Characters and Animations:[/b] Each character and animation will be redone to meet our current quality standards.
[/olist]

[h3]Importing Original Data into Unity
[/h3]
In the video below, you will discover how the import of a scene from the original game is reproduced in Unity. Please [b]activate subtitles[/b] to understand what hides behind the hood.

In this video, we are showing the tool we developed to import the data of the original game. We don’t use the original textures in the final game. It’s only to help us in our development.

[previewyoutube=zIPwAZCTAL4;full][/previewyoutube]

In our next article, we will explain the challenge of geographical continuity.

See you soon!

notes.title: Reboot, remaster or remake? The answer
notes.content:
Dear community,

As promised, it’s high time to explain our project in detail. Since the creation of our studio in 2021, our vision has always been to bring the Little Big Adventure series back to life.

[h2]The Abandoned [i]Reboot[/i]
[/h2]
Our initial ambition was to reinvent the story of Twinsen through a [i]reboot[/i]: discovering his origins, his powers, and his entry into this extraordinary universe. With the invaluable support of Didier and Fred, we redefined this universe, without constraints and for 18 months, integrating:

[list]
[*] A new gameplay
[*] A new camera
[*] A new story
[*] A unique biome and story per island
[*] A new artistic direction
[/list]

[h2]The Evolution Towards The [i]Remaster[/i]
[/h2]
Faced with the difficulties of convincing a publisher for the [i]reboot[/i], we announced the project of remastering the original games. This project – less risky – was intended to reassure publishers about the potential of the license. By [i]remaster[/i], we mean the original game with mainly graphical improvements. For a while, the [i]reboot[/i] and the [i]remaster[/i] coexisted.

Unfortunately, the [i]reboot[/i] project did not convince. We found ourselves with a [i]remaster[/i] project that didn’t really excite us. After working on a [i]reboot[/i] free of many constraints, the return to reality was difficult. We then decided to modify this project to arrive at what will be released: the [i]remake[/i].

[h2]The Alchemy of the [i]Remake[/i]
[/h2]
Thus, the [i]remake[/i] project was born, merging the best of our initial ideas and classic elements of the series. This [i]remake[/i] of [i]Twinsen’s Little Big Adventure Classic[/i] originally made in 1994 will integrate:

[list]
[*] A smoother gameplay
[*] A modernized main storyline
[*] The geographical continuity of outdoor scenes
[*] A reinvented artistic direction
[*] The improvements from TLBA2 Classic
[*] A harmonization between TLBA1 and TLBA2
[/list]

Other changes and novelties are planned, but we will talk about them later.

We hope this article answers your questions and clarifies our intentions.

[h2]Your Involvement
[/h2]
What are your expectations for this [i]remake[/i]? What elements would you like to see integrated or improved? Your passion and suggestions guide us in this adventure.

As a result, the game’s name is now [i]Twinsen’s Little Big Adventure[/i].

To support us, add the game to your wishlist and share it with your friends. Thank you!

notes.title: Great news!
notes.content:
Dear Community,

We have been silent since the pre-alpha playtest this summer, but for a very good reason: negotiations with publishers! This crucial step requires meticulously presenting our project, having several exchanges, and agreeing on details. Once an agreement is reached, drafting the contract adds to our already intense work on the game.

Today, after months of hard work behind the scenes, we are thrilled to share a great piece of news: we have a publisher! Twinsen is (really) back!

Our first collaboration will be the [i]remake[/i] of [i]Twinsen’s Little Big Adventure Classic[/i]. (And yes, you read that right: a remake! We will reveal more details in an upcoming article.)

But then who is this mysterious publisher? For now, we are keeping the information under wraps. Why this discretion? To answer that, it’s important to clarify the role of the publisher for our specific project. Apart from financing the team, our publisher aims to reach new players unfamiliar with Twinsen. To do this, certain industry codes must be respected. For instance, when a publisher makes an announcement, it’s through a cinematic trailer or by showing a part of the game in its final quality. As we have nothing yet to present in final quality, a full announcement seems premature.

Furthermore, since the start of this adventure in September 2021, we’ve made numerous announcements without always having concrete things behind them. This intentional choice (and mostly successful) is no longer desirable today.

We will therefore resume sharing the behind-the-scenes of this adventure with you, the fans, while letting our publisher handle presenting the game to the broadest audience at the ideal time.

We thank you immensely for your patience and unwavering support during these first two years. It has sometimes been difficult, but now we can look forward and move together towards the grand return of [b]Twinsen[/b]!

Dears Twinsunians,

We are thrilled to announce the opening of our pre-alpha playtest! 

The aim of this playtest is to gather your valuable insights and feedback on the game, helping us to fine-tune it and create a gaming experience that truly resonates with our player community. This is your chance to contribute directly to the game's development process and to help shape its future.

To participate, click on "Request access" on the Steam page and you will be granted access automatically.

Once in, you'll be able to explore our game in its early stages, discover new features, and contribute to its improvement.

Upon the conclusion of the playtest, we encourage you to complete a feedback form to let us know your thoughts. Your suggestions and comments will be instrumental in guiding our ongoing development efforts. You have until July 31st to test. 

Thank you for your ongoing support and enthusiasm. We are eager to have you on board and can't wait to hear what you think about our game.

See you on the other side!

Ben
